page: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-3xL40S is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine deployed on the KVM hypervisor. The compute foundation consists of 20 shared vCPUs mapped to 20 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The CPU architecture supports advanced vector instruction sets including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16 alongside 64 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. System memory totals 256 GB, providing an allocation of 12.8 GB per vCPU.

Hardware acceleration is supplied by three NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPUs delivering a cumulative 144 GB of VRAM. Local disk storage is not bundled with this configuration, requiring external network-attached storage solutions to manage disk persistence and filesystem requirements. Network provisioning includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-thread throughput, with Geekbench single-core scoring 3088.0, stress-ng single-core reaching 4190.38, and single-threaded gzip compression achieving 38.86 GB/sec. Multi-threaded performance sits within the upper 25 percent tier, reflected by a PassMark CPU score of 62711.03 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 360.55 GB/sec. System memory bandwidth registers 306.94 GB/sec for uncached reads and 144.32 GB/sec for large block writes, supporting high-throughput database operations and Redis rates of 81.97 million operations per second.

The density of 144 GB VRAM alongside 256 GB of system RAM provides high resource density for parallel compute tasks. The principal operational tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation model and the absence of onboard NVMe storage, meaning disk I/O performance relies entirely on network attached volumes. This server configuration fits large-scale deep learning inference pipelines, GPU-accelerated video transcoding, 3D rendering clusters, and parallel scientific modeling workloads.
description: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-3xL40S is a GPU-accelerated instance featuring 20 shared vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9575F x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz paired with 256 GB of RAM. The instance incorporates three NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPUs providing a total of 144 GB of VRAM. Benchmark data exhibits top-tier single-core CPU throughput, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 3088.0, and strong multi-core performance with a PassMark CPU score of 62711.03. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 306.94 GB/sec. Local disk storage is not bundled with the instance, requiring network-attached storage for persistent workloads. The configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. With 12.8 GB of system memory per core and substantial aggregate GPU memory, this server is configured for multi-GPU inference, high-density graphics rendering, visual computing pipelines, and parallel data science calculations.
